meta.title: Brevard County — the money trail
meta.grand_total_note: The total operating and capital budget the Board of County Commissioners adopted on September 22, 2026, for the year that began October 1 (Resolution No. 26-091).
meta.note: Florida counties count every fund in one total — including reserves (money set aside, not spent this year), money moved between funds, and internal insurance pools — so the total is far larger than what the county spends in a year. Departments below are the July proposal from the county’s own line-item spreadsheets; the adopted book isn’t posted yet. The part the spreadsheets don’t itemize, mostly the elected officers led by the Sheriff, is shown as one computed line.

nodes.note: Computed, not printed: the adopted total ($2,425,831,993) minus everything the county’s line-item spreadsheets itemize ($2,126,414,168). The spreadsheets have no files for the “Charter Officers” — the Sheriff (who runs the jail), Clerk of Court, Tax Collector, Property Appraiser and Supervisor of Elections — and they show the July proposal, before the Board’s changes. The adopted budget book is “coming soon” on the county’s site (Docket #1). The Sheriff alone asked for $206,465,773 for FY2025-26.
nodes.name: Not itemized yet: the elected officers’ budgets and later changes

nodes.note: A separate government with its own elected School Board — and the largest part of most tax bills: 6.31 mills in 2025 (3.062 set by the state, 0.748 local, 1.5 for buildings, 1.0 voter-approved for teacher pay). One mill raises about $82.9 million. Its budget isn’t ingested yet (Docket #3).
nodes.name: Brevard Public Schools

nodes.note: Each sets its own budget and tax rate. 421,144 people live in them; 237,303 live in unincorporated Brevard, where the county provides local services. Melbourne Beach’s budget is fully ingested — see Cities & towns.
